simple.meaning: שָׁמֵם (shâmêm) is a Hebrew action word meaning “ruined.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in 2 Samuel, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel, beginning at 2 Samuel 13:20. The surrounding contexts include family, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁמֵם (H8076) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁמֵם (shâmêm) / H8076 is traced through 2 Samuel 13:20, Jeremiah 12:11, Lamentations 1:13, Lamentations 3:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8076. shamem שָׁמֵם adjective devastated ; — ׳שׁ of sanctuary Dan 9:17 ; feminine שְׁמֵמָה of land Jer 12:11 .

occurrences.englishText: Absalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother. Don’t take this thing to heart.”
They have made it a desolation.
“From on high has he sent fire into my bones,
He has turned away my ways,

therefore, you mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord Yahweh: The Lord Yahweh says to the mountains and to the hills, to the watercourses and to the valleys, to the desolate wastes and to the cities that are forsaken, which have become a prey and derision to the residue of the nations that are all around;
“Now therefore, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant, and to his petitions, and cause your face to shine on your sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord’s sake.
